documents.source_category: Errata to the Annual Report as at 31st March 2026
Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis. Same period as GROUP row -- see GROUP row's notes for shared context (segmental note, cash-flow-comparative caveat, borrowings convention). Company has no discontinued-operations line (held/reported only at Group level), so profit_before_tax (290.04) - tax_expense (76.19) = profit_after_tax (213.85) ties EXACTLY here, unlike the Group row. eps_basic=0.44, only one EPS line given, eps_diluted mirrors it. short_term_borrowings=6,318.52 = 'Loans and borrowings' current only -- Company balance sheet shows a dash (nil) for Bank overdrafts (unlike Group's 339.97), so no overdraft component here. long_term_borrowings=0, same reasoning as Group (no non-current borrowings line). shares_in_issue=487,500,000 -- same share register as Group (AgStar PLC's own issued capital; Company statements are the parent entity's standalone figures). Identity check: total_liabilities (7,755.43) + total_equity (7,693.89) = 15,449.32 = total_assets, ties exactly.

AgStar PLC (AGST), agri-inputs distributor/manufacturer (Materials/Agriculture), FYE 31 March. GROUP basis. Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026) vs Q1 FY2025/26 (three months ended 30 June 2025) comparative -- both explicitly presented as 'Three months ended 30th June: 2026 Un-audited / 2025 Un-audited' on the face P&L (page 2), a genuine same-quarter YoY compare. profit_after_tax=199.64 is the filing's bottom-line 'Profit/(loss) for the period' (i.e. continuing 199.66 LESS a small discontinued-operations net loss of 0.02); profit_before_tax=275.85 is 'Profit/(loss) before tax' from CONTINUING operations only (no separate PBT line for discontinued ops is given) -- this is why PBT(275.85)-tax(76.19)=199.66 does not exactly equal reported PAT of 199.64 (0.02 variance, i.e. the discontinued-ops loss, not an error). eps_basic=0.41 -- filing gives only one EPS line ('Basic earnings/(loss) per share'), no separate diluted figure, so eps_diluted mirrors it. finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- only a single net 'Net finance income/(costs)' line (-52.66) is disclosed, no gross split. shares_in_issue=487,500,000 (461,289,465 voting + 26,210,535 non-voting per Note 3 Stated Capital). short_term_borrowings=6,658.49 = 'Loans and borrowings' current (6,318.52) PLUS 'Bank overdrafts' (339.97), both explicit current-liability lines, combined as both are short-term interest-bearing debt; long_term_borrowings=0 -- no borrowings line at all in non-current liabilities (only Employee benefits, Deferred tax liabilities, Lease liability). inventory=3,196.87 ('Inventories'); trade_receivables=4,253.04 ('Trade and other receivables') -- excludes the separately-disclosed 'Subsidy receivable' (389.51) and 'Amount due from related companies' (1,283.88) lines, kept out per line-item discipline. trade_payables=402.13 ('Trade and other payables') -- excludes 'Amount due to related companies' (56.41) and 'Current tax liabilities' (85.90), both separate lines. SEGMENTAL NOTE (Note 2, page 7): two reportable segments -- Trading (directly imported/resold items) and Non-trading (further-processed items). No segment assets/liabilities/PBT are disclosed (only revenue/cost of sales/gross profit by segment; the Executive Board does not review segment-level PBT/assets per the note). CAUTION on the cash flow statement (page 6): its comparative column is headed '2025 / Audited' rather than '2025 / Un-audited three months ended 30 June' -- the magnitudes (e.g. Group Depreciation 238.75 for '2025' vs 41.17 for the current quarter; Group operating cash flow -1,925.31 for '2025' vs 669.26 current quarter) are far too large to be a single quarter and are consistent instead with the FULL YEAR ended 31 March 2026 audited cash flow being mislabelled '2025' -- i.e. the cash flow statement's 'comparative' is NOT the prior-year same quarter, unlike the P&L and balance sheet. Accordingly only the CURRENT period (three months ended 30 June 2026, Un-audited) cash flow columns are used here; no cash flow YoY comparison is presented in interim_updates for this reason. cash_from_operations=500.10 ('Net cash flow generated from operating activities', Group); capex=12.70 = 'Acquisition of property, plant and equipment' (9.72) + 'Addition to work in progress' (2.98); cash_from_investing=101.53 (net cash USED in investing activities is reported as a positive inflow figure in the filing's own sign convention -- taken as printed); cash_from_financing=386.67. Identity check: total_liabilities (8,197.86) + total_equity (8,435.79) = 16,633.65 = total_assets, ties exactly. EPS 0.41 = 199.64mn / 487.5mn shares = 0.4096, ties.

thesis.thesis_text: AgStar PLC is an agri-inputs distributor/manufacturer (Materials sector) operating Trading and Non-trading segments, FYE 31 March. In its first interim quarter on file (Q1 FY2026/27, ended 30 June 2026), Group PAT grew 267% YoY to Rs.199.64mn on Revenue of Rs.4,639.65mn (+30.4%), driven mainly by sharp gross-margin expansion in the smaller Non-trading segment (14.8% to 23.4%). At Rs.12.40, the stock trades on a run-rate P/E of ~7.6x and P/B of ~0.68x -- statistically cheap -- but an effective tax rate that nearly tripled (11.4% to 27.6%) and short-term borrowings that more than doubled YoY (Rs.6,658.49mn) both warrant monitoring before concluding the growth pace is sustainable (Q1 FY2026/27 interim, source_doc_id 52546).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/news/agriculture-sector data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). This is AGST's first and only interim financial_statements entry -- there is no prior quarter for QoQ comparison, no annual report reviewed, and no dividend/shareholder history in this database, so confidence in this thesis is deliberately set low. The P/E cited is a run-rate approximation (single quarter's EPS x4), not a trailing-twelve-month figure, and should be treated as indicative only.

financial_quality.rationale: Group Q1 FY2026/27 PAT of Rs.199.64mn on Revenue of Rs.4,639.65mn implies a run-rate ROE of approximately 9.5% (annualized PAT of ~Rs.798.6mn / total equity Rs.8,435.79mn) -- a single-quarter approximation only. Net margin expanded sharply to 4.30% from 1.53% YoY and operating margin more than doubled to 7.08% from 2.87%, but effective tax rate jumped from 11.4% to 27.6%, a normalization that caused PAT growth (267%) to trail PBT growth (348%) by a wide margin -- a genuine earnings-quality flag. Short-term borrowings (Rs.6,658.49mn, all of AGST's interest-bearing debt is short-term) more than doubled YoY, funding working capital for a Trading-heavy distribution model.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue +30.4% YoY (Rs.4,639.65mn vs Rs.3,556.97mn) and PAT +267% YoY (Rs.199.64mn vs Rs.54.36mn), driven primarily by sharp gross-margin expansion in the smaller Non-trading (further-processed) segment, from 14.8% to 23.4%, pushing segment gross profit up 137.9% to Rs.308.19mn -- now roughly matching the larger Trading segment's Rs.308.62mn gross profit despite about a third of the revenue. This is a single quarter of data with no prior-quarter (QoQ) comparison available, and the margin gain is concentrated in one segment rather than broad-based, raising a real question of how repeatable it is once tax and finance-cost normalization catches up.

valuation.rationale: At price Rs.12.40 (as of 2026-08-28), run-rate annualized EPS of ~Rs.1.64 (quarterly Group EPS 0.41 x4, an approximation since only one interim quarter exists) implies a P/E of ~7.6x. Market cap of Rs.5,719.99mn against total equity of Rs.8,435.79mn (Group) implies a P/B of ~0.68x -- both statistically cheap for a business growing PAT at 267% YoY, though no dividend has yet been recorded in this database for AGST (a gap) and the P/E is a run-rate approximation, not a trailing-twelve-month figure.

business_quality.rationale: AgStar is an established agri-inputs distributor/manufacturer (Materials sector) operating two segments -- Trading (directly imported/resold items, 71.6% of Group revenue this quarter) and Non-trading (further-processed items) -- providing some diversification within agri-inputs, though the business is fundamentally a low-margin distribution model (Group net margin only 4.30% even after this quarter's improvement) reliant on short-term borrowing to fund inventory and receivables (Rs.3,196.87mn inventory + Rs.4,253.04mn trade receivables against Rs.2,694.96mn cash).

governance_risk.rationale: No credit rating, board/ownership disclosures, or circulars feed exists in this project to assess AGST independently; the only visible signal this quarter is a sharp, unexplained swing in effective tax rate (11.4% to 27.6%) with no note clarifying the cause, and the filing's own cash flow statement mislabels its comparative column (headed 'Audited 2025' but consistent with full-year, not quarterly, magnitudes) -- a disclosure-quality wrinkle in the source filing itself, not a data-entry error on this project's part.

key_reasons: Group PAT grew 267% YoY to Rs.199.64mn on 30.4% revenue growth, with Non-trading segment gross margin expanding from 14.8% to 23.4%
Run-rate P/E of ~7.6x and P/B of ~0.68x are statistically cheap given the pace of profit growth
Effective tax rate jumped from 11.4% to 27.6% YoY, a normalization that caused PAT growth to trail PBT growth (348%) meaningfully
watch_factors: Only one interim quarter is on file -- no QoQ trend, no annual report, and no dividend history exists yet to corroborate the growth story
Short-term borrowings more than doubled YoY to Rs.6,658.49mn (all of AGST's debt is short-term), funding a working-capital-heavy Trading/distribution model
Margin gains this quarter were concentrated in the smaller Non-trading segment -- unclear if repeatable once tax and finance-cost normalization fully plays out

horizon_notes.6m: Next interim result will show whether Non-trading segment margin gains (14.8%->23.4%) hold or reverse, and whether the effective tax rate stabilizes near 27.6% or reverts lower.
horizon_notes.1y: If margin expansion proves durable and short-term borrowing costs are managed, the cheap run-rate multiples (P/E ~7.6x, P/B ~0.68x) could re-rate; a reversal in Non-trading margins would remove the main growth driver.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether AgStar can sustain double-digit revenue growth in agri-inputs distribution while controlling reliance on short-term debt for working capital.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/agriculture-sector or FX data source in this project to assess multi-year input-cost or currency exposure for an agri-inputs importer/distributor.

interim_updates.note_text: AgStar PLC (AGST) reported Group Profit After Tax of Rs.199.64mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 267% YoY from Rs.54.36mn, on Group Revenue of Rs.4,639.65mn, up 30% YoY (2025: Rs.3,556.97mn). By segment (Note 2): Trading segment revenue (directly imported/resold items) grew 23.9% to Rs.3,322.38mn (2025: Rs.2,682.41mn) with gross profit up 42.8% to Rs.308.62mn (2025: Rs.216.10mn, margin 9.29% vs 8.06%); Non-trading segment revenue (further-processed items) grew faster at 50.6% to Rs.1,317.27mn (2025: Rs.874.56mn), and its gross profit surged 137.9% to Rs.308.19mn (2025: Rs.129.51mn) as segment gross margin expanded sharply from 14.8% to 23.4% -- margin expansion in the smaller Non-trading segment, not the larger Trading segment, was the standout driver of the Group's 78% jump in total gross profit (Rs.616.93mn vs Rs.345.61mn). Distribution expenses rose 19.8% to Rs.63.47mn and Administration expenses rose 15.5% to Rs.238.16mn (2025: Rs.52.97mn and Rs.206.17mn respectively), both growing well below the pace of gross profit, so Operating profit more than tripled to Rs.328.51mn (2025: Rs.102.08mn, +222%). Net finance costs worsened 29.8% to Rs.52.66mn (2025: Rs.40.56mn), consistent with a larger short-term borrowings base (Group short-term borrowings, including bank overdrafts, stood at Rs.6,658.49mn at 30 June 2026 vs Rs.3,110.36mn a year earlier). Income tax expense jumped 987% YoY to Rs.76.19mn (2025: Rs.7.01mn) as the effective tax rate rose sharply to 27.6% (2025: 11.4%), which meant PAT growth (266% for continuing operations) trailed the 348% PBT growth by a wide margin -- tax normalisation was a meaningful drag on the bottom line even as operating performance improved dramatically. Company (standalone) PAT grew similarly, +265% YoY to Rs.213.85mn (2025: Rs.58.66mn), on Company revenue +40% YoY to Rs.4,440.75mn -- Company revenue and gross profit (+124% to Rs.549.95mn) both grew faster than Group, implying AgStar's subsidiaries grew more slowly than the parent company itself this quarter. No segment-level PBT, assets or liabilities are disclosed (the Executive Board does not review segments at that level of detail per Note 2), so segment attribution here is limited to revenue and gross profit.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to 30 June 2026 has been collected for AGST -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Segment-level PBT, assets and liabilities are NOT disclosed -- Note 2 states these are not reviewed by the Executive Board on a regular basis, so only segment revenue and gross profit could be cited; this is a genuine filing-level information gap, not a data-entry omission. No cash flow YoY comparison is included: the cash flow statement's 'comparative' column is labelled 'Audited' with magnitudes consistent with the FULL YEAR ended 31 March 2026 rather than the prior-year same quarter (unlike the P&L and balance sheet, which do give a clean same-quarter comparative) -- flagged in detail in the GROUP row's notes field. finance_costs/finance_income are not split (only a net line is given), so no gross interest income/expense figures are stored or compared.
interim_updates.takeaway: AgStar's 267% YoY PAT growth to Rs.199.64mn was driven primarily by sharp gross margin expansion in the smaller Non-trading (further-processed) segment -- margin up from 14.8% to 23.4%, pushing segment gross profit up 137.9% to Rs.308.19mn, roughly matching the larger Trading segment's gross profit in absolute terms. This operating improvement was partly offset at the PAT line by a near-tripling of the effective tax rate (11.4% to 27.6%) and a 29.8% rise in net finance costs on a larger short-term borrowings base -- both worth monitoring, since normalising tax and funding costs mean PAT growth is unlikely to keep pace with the 222% operating profit growth if margin gains from the Non-trading segment level off.

yoy.label: Profit for the period (Group, incl. discontinued ops)

operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.4,639.65mn, +30% YoY (2025: Rs.3,556.97mn); Group Operating profit Rs.328.51mn, +222% YoY; Group PAT Rs.199.64mn, +267% YoY.

Trading segment revenue +23.9% YoY to Rs.3,322.38mn, gross margin 9.29% (2025: 8.06%); Non-trading segment revenue +50.6% YoY to Rs.1,317.27mn, gross margin expanded sharply to 23.4% (2025: 14.8%) -- Non-trading gross profit +137.9% YoY to Rs.308.19mn, nearly matching Trading's Rs.308.62mn despite roughly a third of the revenue.
Income tax expense +987% YoY to Rs.76.19mn (2025: Rs.7.01mn); effective tax rate rose to 27.6% (2025: 11.4%), the main reason PAT growth (266% continuing ops) trailed PBT growth (348%).
Net finance costs (Group) worsened 29.8% YoY to Rs.52.66mn (2025: Rs.40.56mn).
Company (standalone) PAT +265% YoY to Rs.213.85mn on Company revenue +40% YoY to Rs.4,440.75mn -- Company grew faster than Group on both revenue and gross profit this quarter.
Group short-term borrowings (loans/borrowings plus bank overdrafts) rose to Rs.6,658.49mn at 30 June 2026 from Rs.3,110.36mn a year earlier; no long-term borrowings on the balance sheet.
key_drivers: Non-trading segment gross margin expanded from 14.8% to 23.4% YoY, driving segment gross profit up 137.9% to Rs.308.19mn (2025: Rs.129.51mn) -- the standout driver of the Group's 78% total gross profit growth, outpacing the Trading segment's 42.8% gross profit growth (Rs.308.62mn vs Rs.216.10mn).
Effective tax rate rose from 11.4% to 27.6% (tax expense +987% YoY to Rs.76.19mn), a meaningful drag that caused PAT growth (266%) to trail PBT growth (348%) for continuing operations.
Net finance costs +29.8% YoY (Rs.52.66mn vs Rs.40.56mn), consistent with Group short-term borrowings more than doubling YoY (Rs.6,658.49mn vs Rs.3,110.36mn at quarter-end).
